key_insight: The paper shows that data storytelling can make interpretable ML explanations easier for non-experts to understand without exposing sensitive data or model details.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical explanation pipeline for AI systems where decision transparency, privacy protection, and user comprehension must be balanced.
method: Defines data storytelling for interpretable machine learning using the DIST Pyramid.
Introduces an I-P-O model and an architecture for "What-if" and "Why-not" explanation generation.
Uses data desensitization plus SHAP and LLMs to generate ABT-style narratives.
evidence_signal: In a Boston Housing case study, 76.4% and 74.3% of respondents found the "What-if" and "Why-not" stories more comprehensible, with higher accessibility scores than traditional SHAP visualizations.
watch_item: The approach may depend on careful prompt/design control so LLM-generated stories remain faithful to model behavior and do not oversimplify explanations.
paper_title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details
